steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure with container and items
steps.instruction: Create a simple HTML file with a container div containing several item divs. Add a container div with the class 'flex-container' and three child divs with the class 'item'.
steps.hint: Start with a basic HTML structure. Inside the body, create a div with class 'flex-container' and nest three divs inside it, each with class 'item'.
steps.analogousExample:
Box 1
Box 2
Box 3
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Flex: Container and Direction</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add your flex container and items here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an HTML file with a container div containing three item divs, ready for applying flexbox styles.
successCriteria: The HTML file contains a div with class 'flex-container' and three child divs with class 'item'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the HTML structure needed for flexbox practice. The container and items are in place.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly three item divs inside the flex-container div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HTML structure is missing or incorrect. Please create a div with class 'flex-container' containing three divs with class 'item'.

steps.title: Add basic styling to visualize the structure
steps.instruction: Open styles.css and add CSS rules to style the body with a background color and add a border to the container element you'll create later.
steps.hint: Use the body selector to set a background color (e.g., light gray) and define a class .container with a border property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS file will have styles that will later apply to the HTML structure, making it easier to see the container and items.
successCriteria: The styles.css file contains a body rule with a background-color and a .container rule with a border property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the basic styling that will help visualize the flex container and items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both the body background color and the .container border.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've written valid CSS rules for both the body and .container selectors.

steps.title: Introduce the display: flex property
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property display: flex to the .container selector to turn it into a flex container.
steps.hint: In your CSS, find the .container rule and add display: flex; inside the curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container element will become a flex container, enabling flexbox layout for its child items.
successCriteria: The .container selector has the property display: flex;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully turned the container into a flex container by adding display: flex.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you added display: flex; to the .container selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .container selector does not have display: flex;. Try adding it inside the .container rule.

steps.title: Observe the default flex direction
steps.instruction: Add the display: flex property to the .container selector to activate flexbox layout.
steps.hint: Set the display property to flex inside the .container rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will become a flex container, and its child items will automatically arrange horizontally in a row (the default flex-direction).
successCriteria: The .container selector has display: flex; property applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've activated flexbox. Notice how the items now arrange horizontally without needing any direction property - that's the default row direction.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're adding display: flex; to the .container selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to add the display: flex; property to make the container a flex container.

steps.title: Apply flex-direction: row explicitly
steps.instruction: Add the flex-direction: row property to the .container class to explicitly set the horizontal layout direction.
steps.hint: Add 'flex-direction: row;' inside the .container rule to specify that flex items should be arranged horizontally.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex container will now explicitly use row direction, arranging items horizontally from left to right.
successCriteria: The .container rule includes flex-direction: row; property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've explicitly set flex-direction: row, which arranges items horizontally. This makes the layout intention clear even though row is the default.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added 'flex-direction: row;' inside the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex-direction property wasn't added correctly. Add 'flex-direction: row;' to the .container rule to explicitly set horizontal layout.

steps.title: Change to flex-direction: column
steps.instruction: In the .container rule, change the flex-direction value from 'row' to 'column'.
steps.hint: Look for the flex-direction property in the .container rule and replace 'row' with 'column'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will stack vertically instead of horizontally.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully changed the flex direction to column, making the items stack vertically.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you've changed the flex-direction value to 'column' in the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex-direction property should be set to 'column' in the .container rule to arrange items vertically.

steps.title: Experiment with flex-direction: row-reverse
steps.instruction: Change the flex-direction value from 'column' to 'row-reverse' in the .container class.
steps.hint: Look for the flex-direction property in your .container class and replace its current value with 'row-reverse'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will be arranged horizontally in reverse order, starting from the right side.
successCriteria: The .container class has flex-direction: row-reverse; applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully changed the flex direction to row-reverse. Notice how the items now flow from right to left instead of left to right.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're changing the flex-direction property value to 'row-reverse' in the .container class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex-direction property should be set to 'row-reverse' in the .container class to reverse the horizontal order of items.

steps.title: Experiment with flex-direction: column-reverse
steps.instruction: Change the flex-direction property from 'column' to 'column-reverse' in the .container rule.
steps.hint: Modify the existing flex-direction value in your CSS. The property should now be 'column-reverse'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will now be arranged vertically from bottom to top, reversing their original order.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully reversed the vertical order of flex items using column-reverse.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're changing the flex-direction property to 'column-reverse' in the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're modifying the existing flex-direction property in the .container rule to use 'column-reverse'.

steps.title: Add more items to see direction behavior with multiple elements
steps.instruction: Add two more .item divs inside your HTML container to see how flex-direction behaves with multiple elements.
steps.hint: Copy and paste the existing .item divs in your HTML to create additional items.
steps.analogousExample:
Item 1
Item 2
Item 3
Item 4
Item 5
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will now have more items, making it easier to observe how different flex-direction values affect the layout of multiple elements.
successCriteria: Your HTML contains at least 5 .item divs inside the .container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Adding more items helps visualize how flex-direction organizes multiple elements.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some items, but try to add at least 5 total items to clearly see the direction behavior.
steps.feedbackWrong: Make sure you're adding more .item divs to your HTML structure, not modifying the CSS.

steps.title: Create a practice exercise with multiple containers
steps.instruction: Add a second container with class 'container2' and set its flex-direction to 'row'.
steps.hint: Create a new CSS rule for .container2 with display: flex and flex-direction: row.
steps.expectedOutcome: A second flex container with horizontal item arrangement will be created for practice.
successCriteria: A .container2 rule exists with display: flex and flex-direction: row.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a second flex container with row direction.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure .container2 has both display: flex and flex-direction: row.
steps.feedbackWrong: The second container isn't properly defined. Create a .container2 rule with display: flex and flex-direction: row.
